I changed nothing this run. The work is healthy, but there isn't enough of it to fill the machine.

- **Running:** 4 FEBio runs (physrotFr2 for p060, p062, p109 and p125). All 4 logs updated in the last 10 s, and they are pinned to separate cores.
- **Progress:** p062 has 5 of its 6 windows done, p125 has 3, p060 has 2. p109 has none.
- **p109:** its extension window stalled at t≈3.52, the same way flexion did earlier. The watchdog stopped it at 20:05, as it is meant to. p109 is now running its LB_right window, and that one is moving forward.
- **Resources:** 8 of 32 cores in use, memory 60 of 128 GB, no out-of-memory kills, no new CPU throttling. None of the 7 GPUs is ours; other users have them. Disk has 1.5 TB free.
- **Queues:** nothing waiting in either queue. In the FEBio queue, 0 jobs finished in the last 3 h; the last one was at 16:40. The new-repo task queue is unchanged at 1 done and 5 failed.
- **Services:** all 6 tmux services are up. The 3 one-off startup jobs in `ops/resume_all.sh` are already finished, so no restart was needed.
- **What limits speed:** lack of queued work. About 24 cores and 68 GB sit idle.

**Needs a person:**
- Queue more work.
- Have the science owner look at the p109 flexion/extension stall in physio_fric2.
- Decide T01, T16, T10 (the scheduler disk guard) and the al_loop gate.

The report is `work/agents/foreman/report_20261102_2026.md`. I also overwrote `status.json` and added one line to `work/ops/foreman_actions.log`.
